title: Event fingerprinting gateway and progressive schema negotiation for usage ingest
creator: Lena Kim
description: Problem: the console metrics pipeline is seeing a rising fraction of malformed or semantically-shifted usage events after product rollout. Existing validators reject too many events at the edge, and downstream pipelines struggle to join events when entity identifiers or minor schema fields evolve. This ticket implements a lightweight event fingerprinting gateway that assigns stable fingerprints to incoming payloads and performs progressive schema negotiation before dropping or routing events. Goals are to improve downstream join fidelity, reduce hard rejections during schema transitions, and provide observability for drift without blocking traffic.
technical_solution_overview: Design a gateway service that runs at the telemetry ingress layer: 1) compute a deterministic 'event_fingerprint' (64-bit hex) based on canonicalized key set (customer_id, session_id if present, timestamp bucket, stable top-level fields). 2) consult the schema registry to determine the event family and nearest compatible schema version. 3) attempt lightweight transformations (field renames, type coercions, minor defaults) via a rules engine; track which transformation rules applied. 4) emit validation result (accept/accept-with-normalization/flag-for-review/reject) and attach metadata (fingerprint, normalized_payload_ref, schema_version, transform_flags). 5) route accepted events to primary pipeline, accept-with-normalization to enriched topic, flagged events to a quarantine stream with sample windows for manual review. The service will be horizontally scalable, written in Go with a small Rust core for canonicalization performance-critical path.
acceptance_criteria: Incoming events are stamped with event_fingerprint for 99.95% of valid payloads
Gateway identifies a compatible schema (or fallback) for >99% of traffic without backpressure
Normalized events maintain checksum compatibility for join keys used by downstream billing and usage aggregations
Rejection rate due to strict schema mismatch drops by >=80% versus baseline during A/B toggles
End-to-end latency added by gateway stays under 15ms p50 and 60ms p99 at steady load
All transformations are logged and reversible for audit (stored in event metadata)
Feature flag allows instant rollback to passthrough validation
design_notes: Fingerprint composition: prefer stable fields, avoid volatile request IDs; allow optional salt per-customer to avoid cross-tenant collisions
Deterministic canonicalization rules (field order, whitespace trimming, numeric normalization) live in a compact WASM policy to enable hot reload without service restart
Progressive negotiation rules expressed as a prioritized list of non-destructive transforms; destructive changes (field drops) must go to quarantine
Use an in-memory LRU cache for recent schema-version lookups with a background refresher to the central registry
Metrics emitted: fingerprint_rate, normalization_rate, rejection_rate_by_reason, transform_rule_counts, schema_fallback_rate
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): route 1% of traffic for two customer cohorts; monitor transform and rejection metrics for 72h
Phase 2 (scale): 10% traffic with auto-escalation if key metrics within thresholds for 48h
Phase 3 (opt-in): expose console toggle for SRE and Platform teams to opt specific projects in
Phase 4 (global): flip default to on and migrate remaining projects over rolling windows
Rollback: feature flag to bypass gateway and write events to legacy topic if any critical metric deviates
testing: Unit tests for canonicalization and fingerprint collision properties
Property-based tests for deterministic transforms across schema versions
Integration tests with schema registry mock verifying fallback behaviors
Load test with synthetic traffic (mixed valid/malformed) up to 30k rps; measure p50/p99 latency and CPU/GPU if applicable
Chaos test: simulate schema registry lag and confirm gateway uses cache + safe fallback path
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: fingerprint coverage, transform rule heatmap, rejection reasons over time
SLOs: <0.2% unexpected rejection; p99 gateway added latency <60ms
Alerts: sustained increase in quarantine volume (>3x baseline for 15m), cache eviction storms, schema registry 5xx errors
